pix/host/cli._prod_loc_note: 475 -> 502: Deps.Config() now warns about config keys this build ignores, so a typo is surfaced instead of silently doing nothing. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget, which is the only way this number is allowed to move.

pix/host/cmd/pix._prod_loc_note: 3036 -> 3071: `pix resume SESSION [DIR]` turns pi's exact exit receipt into a host command without exposing `run -- --session`. Then 3071 -> 3136, edges 22 -> 23: `pix reset` is back (reset_cmd.go). The new edge is cmd/pix -> workflow/reset, and it is the whole point of the shape: reset is L3 and workflow/launch is its L3 sibling, so the command layer is the ONLY place allowed to hold both. It injects `pix rm --all` into reset as reset.Sweep rather than letting reset grow a sandbox removal of its own; that alternative would have cost no edge here and created a second bulk force-removal seam beside the one explicitly-named one. Deliberate, reviewed raises of a shrink-only budget.

pix/host/config._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 796 -> 804: ServiceEnabled now resolves `services` the way `pix-host serve` does, and the load-bearing half is that EMPTY MEANS ALL (resolveServices: "an empty result means all"). Reading empty as none made doctor call memory OPTIONAL on a config where serve starts it -- the commonest config there is -- so a memory unit that was genuinely down could not fail readiness. A deliberate, reviewed raise.

pix/host/health._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 1277 -> 1286, globals 29 -> 30: the probe half of McpAuthNotRequired (see pix/host/mcp's note) -- a server that needs no OAuth is now reported as ANSWERED rather than counted against the row as unproven, which is what made the mcp row a permanent `?`. Carried with the earlier raise in this package: prod_loc 1254 -> 1277: the mcp row's evidence was ONE run-on line -- eight servers, each with its own parenthetical, joined into several hundred characters that no one can read in a terminal or skim anywhere. A reader could not tell how many servers there were, which one was theirs, or where one note ended. writeEvidence now gives a set-valued evidence string one line per item under a count, and the notes are joined with newlines because "; " cannot be the separator: the notes contain semicolons, and splitting on those turned 8 servers into 16 half-sentences. Single-item evidence is untouched, so every other row reads exactly as before. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget. Then prod_loc 1286 -> 1456, globals 30 -> 34: doctor stopped treating "registered with the gateway" as "working". MCPServer gained Undeclared/Command/Probe and a LookPath seam, and checkServer gained four real questions it never asked: does the declared command still resolve, does any active pack still declare this name, does the server's own probe pass, and did the probe actually get to run. Per-server checks also became concurrent, because the budget is per-probe and one `op run` blocking on a locked vault used to starve every check after it and report gaps that were never measured. This is the change: the previous cheapness WAS the bug — an eight-server host read `✓ 8 registered` while two of those registrations pointed at commands that no longer existed.

pix/host/inference._prod_loc_note: raised together for ONE change: `pix doctor` and `pix setup` demanded an anthropic/openai/google key from hosts whose models need none. A pack's sbx-session backends carry their own credential (a Docker login session the sbx proxy injects inside the sandbox, unreplayable from the host by design), so the key store lists nothing and the required row went red prescribing `pix models add anthropic` -- a key nothing would read. `pix run`'s launch gate already skipped the key check on exactly this host (inference.ConfiguredKeylessInference); ProviderKeyProbe.Keyless + inference.KeylessBackends give the same carve-out to the two verbs that lacked it, so all three stop disagreeing about one host. Distinct from Callable, which answers "this key routes nowhere"; Keyless answers "no key was ever the credential". provision's new edge is importing inference for that one predicate rather than re-deriving a second opinion. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget.

pix/host/mcp._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 1033 -> 1050, exports 28 -> 29, globals 18 -> 19: ONE outcome, McpAuthNotRequired. `sbx mcp auth status` answers "does not require OAuth" for a server whose credentials come from the gateway's op-refs injection rather than an OAuth broker (slack, google-docs-create). The parser had buckets only for authorized and failed, so a DEFINITE answer fell through to unknown and `pix doctor` carried a permanent `?` that no action could ever clear -- which teaches a reader to stop reading the glyph, the same way a fix that cannot fix anything teaches them to stop reading fixes. The new case is matched BEFORE the negatives, because "does not require oauth" contains "not". A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget.

pix/host/packinfo._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 942 -> 1215, exports 32 -> 37, globals 4 -> 6: the pack manifest grew the two things that make a pack checkable. Integrations gained a transport (command/args/probe alongside image/manifest/url) so every declared server names something that can actually be started, and setup steps gained a declarative require/apply vocabulary with fail-closed validation. Most of the added lines are that validation. It buys the defect class outright: the previous shell hooks called `pix` verbs that had been deleted, so a pack's setup could never pass, and nothing detected it until a user tried to onboard. A pack that names no commands cannot be broken by a CLI change.

pix/host/secret._prod_loc_note: 1240 -> 1290, exports 42 -> 43, globals 8 -> 9: web-search TOOL keys (ToolKeyRefOrder) are now seeded/checked/mirrored like model-provider keys, but held OUT of ProviderKeyRefOrder and ModelProviders so `pix models add` never offers a name it would reject and a missing search key can never refuse a launch. The new export is the list itself; the new global is the sync map, now DERIVED from both lists so an entry cannot be added to one and forgotten in the other. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget. Then prod_loc 1290 -> 1306, exports 43 -> 44: the non-secret allowlist became a parameter (secret.NonSecret) instead of a hardcoded map of one vendor's three GOG_* variables. Pix now allowlists nothing of its own; the set is exactly what the active pack declares as env_keys, so a pack that needs a plain-text variable is the thing that authorizes it and deactivating that pack takes its allowances with it.

pix/host/service._prod_loc_note: 1664 -> 1708: `serve stop` now sweeps for orphaned `pix-host serve` processes AFTER stopping the pid its pidfile recorded. A pidfile names one daemon and is not proof there is only one, so a second daemon outliving its own pidfile kept holding :11435 while stop reported success. That is why `pix serve stop` had to be run twice. The sweep only ever signals pids that positively verify as our live serve. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget.

pix/host/workflow/launch._prod_loc_note: 2458 -> 2503, exports 109 -> 112: personal context (skills + standing AGENTS.md) is now mounted unconditionally at the context ROOT, so a session can write its FIRST skill from inside the sandbox and keep the whole dir in git. Previously the mount was gated on the dir already having entries, which made the first skill impossible to author in-sandbox, and only skills/ was mounted, so AGENTS.md was invisible. New exports: MountDirs (the mount set, now distinct from the skill set), PersonalSkillsDir (one spelling shared by loader and mount), EnsurePersonalContextDir. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget. Then 2503 -> 2543, globals 42 -> 43: teardown now translates pi's parting "To resume this session: pi --session-dir ..." into the host command that actually works (`pix run -- -c`), and only when a session file provably exists. Suppressing pi's line would have been wrong: .pi-sessions is in the workspace mount, so the session genuinely outlives the sandbox; only the dialect was unusable.

pix/host/workflow/models._prod_loc_note: 1084 -> 1091: `models add` no longer tells the user to run `pix models route`. That was busywork presented as a required step: every `pix run` already recompiles the intent map from current bindings. The line now states that routing updates itself. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget.

pix/host/workflow/pack._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 3049 -> 3062, globals 4 -> 5: ONE seam, paying for itself many times over. propagateConfig's real implementation runs `launchctl kickstart -k` against the developer's own pix LaunchAgent, and every test here that adopts a pack went through it -- so a test run restarted the live daemon on the machine running it, serially, blocking on each. That was 507s of a 578s `go test ./...` locally against a fast gate whose own documented go-test baseline is 32.8s; CI never saw it because there is no agent there to kick. Behind the var, this package is 2.8s and the whole gate is 47s instead of 9.5 minutes. The new global IS the seam. A deliberate, reviewed raise. Then prod_loc 3062 -> 3166: the declarative setup runner (checkRequires/applySteps) plus rendering require/apply on the Tier-1 consent screen. The screen is not optional detail — a declarative step still names binaries and argv that run on this Mac, so consenting means seeing them, and summarising them as a count would be the same failure as the registration that read "ready" for a command that did not exist.
